Biological materials

In order to obtain the fungal mycelial mass required for DNA extraction, place four mycelial plugs (6 mm in diameter) in 500 mL of potato dextrose broth (PDB) and grow for 7–14 days shaking at 140 rpm on an orbital shaker in a growth cabinet protected from light, at 22 °C.

To reach the required gDNA concentration, up to 1 g of flash-frozen mycelium is required. When enough mycelium for the extraction plus backup material has grown, harvest ~3 g of mycelium using a 0.22 μm bottle top filter and vacuum pump.
Rinse the mycelium with sterilized purified water to remove any residue of PDB.
Cut agar plugs from the harvested mycelium and place them in an autoclave bag. Flash freeze the harvested material in liquid nitrogen and store in a -80 °C freezer until ready to process. A
Thaw the required amount of RNase A and Proteinase K on ice, if kept frozen.
Pre-cool freshly aliquoted propanol-2-OL in freezer at -20 °C.
Pre-cool freshly aliquoted chloroform in freezer at -20 °C.
Make up a fresh batch of 70% EtOH.
Ensure mortars and pestles have been cleaned and sterilized in an autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Gather reagents and supplies
steps.instruction: Collect all reagents, solutions, and labware listed for both methods, including Cytiva Nucleon PhytoPure kit (catalog RPN8511), Propanol‑2‑OL (Merck, cat 33539‑2.5LM), chloroform (Merck, cat 32211‑2.5LM), ethanol (VWR, cat 01000940), RNase A (Invitrogen, cat 10618703), Proteinase K (Thermo, cat 11501515), Low‑TE buffer (Fisher, cat 10647633), potato dextrose broth (Formedium, cat PDB0102), Qubit assays (Invitrogen, cat Q23854 and Q32853), 70 % EtOH (made fresh), 2 mL LoBind Eppendorf tubes (cat 10031282), filter tips, medical wipes, 0.22 µm bottle‑top filter (cat 15993307), dry ice, autoclave, and for the Macherey‑Nagel method the NucleoBond HMW DNA kit (cat 740160.20) with buffers H1‑H5, HE elution buffer, RNase A, Proteinase K, 50 mL Falcon tubes (cat 430790), disposable pipettes, etc.

steps.title: Grow fungal mycelium
steps.instruction: Place four 6 mm mycelial plugs in 500 mL potato dextrose broth, incubate 7–14 days at 22 °C, shaking 140 rpm on an orbital shaker in a light‑protected cabinet.

steps.title: Harvest and rinse mycelium
steps.instruction: When sufficient growth is achieved, harvest ~3 g of mycelium using a 0.22 µm bottle‑top filter and vacuum pump; rinse the harvested mycelium with sterilized purified water to remove broth residues.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze mycelium
steps.instruction: Cut agar plugs from the harvested mycelium, place them in an autoclave bag, flash‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C until extraction.

steps.title: Thaw enzymes and pre‑cool solvents
steps.instruction: On ice, thaw RNase A and Proteinase K; pre‑cool aliquoted propanol‑2‑OL and chloroform at –20 °C; prepare a fresh batch of 70 % EtOH; autoclave mortars and pestles at 121 °C for 15 min; collect dry ice in a polystyrene box in the fume hood; pre‑heat Cytiva Reagent 1 to 50 °C.

steps.title: Grind mycelium for Cytiva method
steps.instruction: Working over dry ice in a fume hood, grind 100 mg flash‑frozen mycelium in a sterilized mortar until a fine talcum‑like powder forms, then transfer to a labeled 2 mL LoBind tube (use 400 mg total in quadruplicate for low‑yielding strains).

steps.title: Lyse cells (Cytiva)
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL pre‑heated Reagent 1 and 20 µL RNase A to the tube, vortex or invert 5–10 times, then incubate 50 °C for 30 min shaking at 450 rpm (extend up to 12 h if needed); add 200 µL Reagent 2 and invert 5–10 times; add 10 µL Proteinase K (30 mg/mL, 600 U/mL) and incubate 65 °C for 1 h shaking at 450 rpm.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA (Cytiva)
steps.instruction: Place tubes on ice for 20 min; add 500 µL pre‑cooled chloroform and 100 µL PhytoPure resin suspension, rotate 10 min at room temperature; centrifuge 1,300 × g for 10 min, transfer the upper aqueous phase (~500 µL) to a new 2 mL tube leaving some behind; add an equal volume of pre‑cooled propanol‑2‑OL, invert 5–10 times, incubate –20 °C for 15 min; centrifuge 4,000 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant and air‑dry the pellet with caps open for 2 min.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet (Cytiva)
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 1 mL 70 % EtOH, invert five times and centrifuge 4,000 × g for 20 min; discard ethanol without disturbing the pellet; repeat the wash two more times (total three washes); air‑dry caps open for 5 min or until no ethanol droplets remain, dabbing large droplets with a sterile medical wipe (avoid the pellet).

steps.title: Resuspend DNA (Cytiva)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 100 µL low‑TE elution buffer; optionally leave the tube overnight at 4 °C for complete dissolution; quantify the next day.

steps.title: Prepare biological material for Macherey‑Nagel
steps.instruction: Use the same harvested mycelium prepared in steps 1–4 (Method 1, step A1).

steps.title: Pre‑heat buffers and chill equipment (Macherey)
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat buffer H1 to 55 °C and set the HC mixer to 55 °C; pre‑chill a sterilized mortar, pestle, measuring spoon, and a labeled 50 mL Falcon tube on dry ice in a polystyrene box placed in the fume hood; prepare fresh 70 % EtOH.

steps.title: Grind mycelium for Macherey method
steps.instruction: Working over dry ice in a fume hood, grind 1 g flash‑frozen mycelium in a sterilized mortar to a fine talcum‑like powder and transfer to a labeled 50 mL Falcon tube; keep on dry ice until lysis.

steps.title: Lyse cells (Macherey)
steps.instruction: Add 2.5 mL pre‑heated lysis buffer H1 and 100 µL Proteinase K to the Falcon tube (scale up proportionally for larger samples), vortex 5 s, then incubate 50 °C for 30 min shaking at 450 rpm (extend up to 12 h if needed).

steps.title: Digest RNA (Macherey)
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL RNase A to the lysate, invert to mix, and incubate 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Set up columns and equilibrate
steps.instruction: Combine a NucleoBond HMW column with a plastic washer on a labeled 50 mL Falcon tube (ensure the washer does not seal the waste vessel); add 12 mL buffer H2 to the upper rim of the column filter to pre‑wet the silica matrix; let gravity flow and discard the flowthrough.

steps.title: Bind DNA to column
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL buffer H2 to the lysate, invert five times, then load the mixture onto the column, allowing lysate to pass by gravity; discard flowthrough; add 6 mL buffer H3 to the column rim, let pass, discard flowthrough and the column filter; wash the column (without filter) with 12 mL buffer H4, discard flowthrough; place the column on a clean labeled 50 mL Falcon tube and elute DNA with 5 mL buffer H5.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA (Macherey)
steps.instruction: Divide the 5 mL eluate into five 2 mL LoBind tubes (1 mL each) using a wide‑bore 1,000 µL tip; add 1 mL chilled propanol‑2‑OL to each tube, invert gently 10 times; spool visible DNA strands onto a labeled tube containing 50 µL Low‑TE or HE buffer using a sterilized glass rod (no wash needed) and store the spooled tube at 4 °C; centrifuge the remaining solution at 5,000 × g for 10 min at room temperature and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet (Macherey)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL 70 % EtOH to each pellet, centrifuge 5,000 × g for 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant completely; add 25 µL 70 % EtOH for a second wash, centrifuge 7,000 × g for 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant; open lids, place tubes upright and dry at room temperature until ethanol evaporates (~5 min), dab any remaining droplets with sterile medical tissue (do not overdry).

steps.title: Resuspend DNA (Macherey)
steps.instruction: Add ≤20 µL low‑TE or HE buffer to each pellet, swirl to immerse; note that 50 µL spooled DNA from step K4 is already present, giving a final volume of ~150 µL; leave tubes overnight at 4 °C for complete resuspension; next morning combine all DNA into the final tube (which already contains the spooled DNA); use wide‑bore tips for all downstream handling.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality
steps.instruction: Measure purity with a NanoDrop (A260/280 and A260/230), quantify concentration with a Qubit HS or BR assay, and evaluate fragment length and integrity using a Femto Pulse analyzer.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: • Hill et al. [1]. Evolutionary genomics reveals variation in structure and genetic content implicated in virulence and lifestyle in the genus Gaeumannomyces. DNA quantity and quality were assessed using three techniques for nucleic acid quantification: UV spectrophotometry using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer, dsDNA specific fluorimetry using a Qubit fluorometer, and DNA integrity and length of strands using a Femto Pulse parallel capillary electrophoresis system. DNA purity was assessed by reading A 260/230nm and A 260/280nm on the NanoDrop instrument ( Table 1 ). When determining the purity of each extraction, it is important to acknowledge the difference between the Qubit DNA concentration readings and the Nanodrop. Differences greater than 5% indicate impurity in the DNA extracts. On average, the Cytiva Nucleon PhytoPure kit produces greater differences than the Macherey-Nagel NucleoBond HMW DNA kit ( Table 1 ). After assessing whether DNA concentration and purity pass minimum requirements, the relative success of each extraction for sequencing is then determined by assessing strand length, which impacts downstream library preparation ( Table 1 ). Samples with a greater proportion of shorter strands (at a cutoff of 40 kbp) are constructed using the 10–15 kb library preparation, and those with a greater proportion of larger strands are constructed using the 15–20 kb library preparation kit. Strand length will impact genome assembly contiguity. However, given the strand lengths attained here and the downstream biological questions, low input DNA extraction and shorter fragment length libraries did not impact our ability to address questions on genome evolution [6] (see Table S2).
